thread.title: Close Update: Apple's Trillion Dollar Valuation Cheers Wall Street

title: Close Update: Apple's Trillion Dollar Valuation Cheers Wall Street
text:
Close Update: Apple's Trillion Dollar Valuation Cheers Wall Street August 02, 2018, 04:29:41 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Wall Street overcame early losses tied to escalating trade war tensions between the US and China as investors cheered upbeat quarterly results from Apple ( AAPL ) and a one trillion dollar valuation for the tech giant.
The Dow closed fractionally lower, but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed higher with technology and consumer staple sectors outperforming.
Encouraging quarterly results continued to pour in on Thursday with upbeat results from Tesla ( TSLA ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ) and Cigna ( CI ) fueling investor optimism and overshadowing a miss from MGM ( MGM ) and Prudential (PRU). Besides Apple, Tesla was the standout among Nasdaq component stocks, lunging 16% higher on a better-than-expected increase in Q2 sales.
The trading day kicked off on the back foot after trade tensions were inflamed by President Donald Trump's threat of a 25% tariff on $200 billion in Chinese goods followed by Beijing's obligatory threat to retaliate. Global bourses were significantly lower overnight with Chinese exchanges down more than 2% and the yuan taking another spill.
After stumbling at the open, the major indices started marching higher in lockstep with Apple's trek toward the $1 trillion milestone. Although the Dow could not breach Wednesday's closing level, the Nasdaq reached 7,800 before stalling and the S&P 500 pierced resistance at 2822.
Economic data took a backseat ahead of Friday's pivotal labor market report. Initial jobless claims were up by just 1,000 in the latest survey week to 218,000, slightly below 220,000 estimates. Factory orders increased 0.7% in June, matching expectations, while orders excluding the transportation sector were up 0.4%. The final durable goods orders for June was revised to +0.8% from +0.1% while ex-transportation was revised to +0.2% from +0.1%.
For Friday, the labor market is expected to report a 190,000 increase in non-farm payrolls for July, driving the jobless rate to 3.9% from 4.0%. The closely watched wage component is expected to increase by 0.3%, though Y-O-Y will likely stay unchanged at 2.7%.
Also scheduled for Friday is the balance of trade for June and the purchasing managers (PMI) and Institute for Supply Management (ISM) services sector indices.
